Where builds go sideways

The price isn't the risk. What happens after you fall in love with a plan is.

Your price guide is the easy part. Here's where custom home projects actually go over budget and off the rails — and why it almost always traces back to a decision made, or skipped, before construction ever starts.

The budget creep

  • The builder's quote comes back tens of thousands over the number in your head
  • "Allowances" you didn't fully understand quietly inflate the total
  • Change orders start stacking up the moment framing begins

The design regret

  • You approve a plan, then realize it doesn't live the way you pictured — once it's expensive to change
  • The layout fights the site, the sun, or the view
  • You're deep into drawings before anyone flags the problem

The permit wall

  • Your submission gets kicked back, and the project stalls for weeks
  • A setback, height limit, or zoning rule surfaces after you've designed around it
  • You're decoding municipal bylaws you've never had to read before

The build surprises

  • Vague drawings mean every contractor quotes a different number — you can't compare
  • Details left off the plans become "extras" you never budgeted for
  • No one's accountable when the design and the build don't match

The timeline drift

  • The build runs months past the promised date — and every extra month costs you rent or interest
  • Trades sit idle waiting on each other because no one's coordinating the sequence
  • A single unanswered detail on the drawings stalls the whole site

The decision overload

  • Hundreds of choices with no framework, so you freeze — or say yes to everything and blow the budget
  • "While we're at it" add-ons quietly pile up
  • You're making structural and technical calls you're not equipped for, and hoping they're right

See the pattern? Not one of these is a building problem — they're all planning problems. Cheap to prevent on paper. Brutal to fix once the concrete's poured.

The path forward

The number above is the easy part. This is the process that protects it — the same six phases, every project. The design you approve is the design that gets built.

Your Path to Built

Six phases. One studio. From your first conversation to your final walkthrough.

We don't hand you drawings and disappear. We stay with your project from the first sketch all the way through the build.

01Initial Consultationwhere it starts
Every project begins with a conversation — your vision, your functional needs, your style, your scope. You walk away with a clear proposal of exactly what we'd do and what comes next. No guesswork about how this works.
◆ The Innova difference
02Bylaw & Code Reviewbefore you design
Before we design a thing, we pressure-test your site against the zoning, setbacks, height limits, and land-use rules. So you never fall in love with a home you're not allowed to build — and the design you approve is the design that gets built. This is why our clients don't get blindsided at the permit office.
03Design Phaseconcepts → drawings
The creative and technical core of your project — where the home takes shape and becomes buildable:
  • Preliminary concepts
  • Design refinement
  • Material & feature planning
  • Full construction drawings
  • Coordination-ready documentation
  • Optional 3D renderings
04Permitting Processwe submit it
We prepare and submit your drawings, coordinate with the municipal departments, and handle the review comments. You don't chase paperwork or wait on hold with the permit office — we run it for you.
05Construction Phasewe stay on it
Once the build begins, we stay involved — site visits, design clarifications, detail review, and problem-solving alongside your build team. The drawings don't just get tossed over the fence.
06Contractor Coordinationthrough to done
We work alongside your contractors from start to finish — providing drawings, clarifications, and design input whenever the build needs it. One team, all the way to your final walkthrough.
Six phases, handled in order — with no surprises in between.

Where home budgets go wrong

Nearly every overrun is a planning problem, not a building problem — cheap to prevent on paper, brutal to fix once the concrete's poured.

  • Budget creep: quotes come back over your number, allowances inflate the total, change orders stack up.
  • Design regret: a plan approved before anyone catches what won't work — or won't fit the site.
  • Permit wall: a setback, height, or zoning rule surfaces after you've designed around it.
  • Build surprises: vague drawings mean uncomparable quotes and "extras" you never budgeted for.

Your Path to Built — how we prevent all of it

  1. Initial Consultation. Your vision, needs, and scope — you leave with a clear proposal.
  2. Bylaw & Code Review. We check zoning, setbacks, and height limits before design, so the design you approve is the design that gets built.
  3. Design Phase. Concepts, refinement, material planning, full construction drawings, coordination docs, optional 3D.
  4. Permitting Process. We prepare, submit, and manage the municipal review for you.
  5. Construction Phase. Site visits, clarifications, and problem-solving with your build team.
  6. Contractor Coordination. Drawings and design input through to your final walkthrough.
